Part three. WeWork. After the failed IPO, WeWork tried to start again. Thousands of jobs were cut. Then, in twenty twenty, the pandemic hit, and offices around the world went empty. In twenty twenty-one, WeWork finally went public anyway, through a deal valuing it at about nine billion dollars, less than a fifth of its old price. But the leases were still there. Long, expensive leases on buildings that people no longer wanted. The shares kept falling, down more than ninety-nine percent. In November twenty twenty-three, WeWork filed for bankruptcy. A company once worth forty-seven billion dollars. Rise... and ruin. Follow for more.
